comparator.name: Computer Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The degree has a 60 EC foundation, 75 EC of advanced compulsory courses, a 15 EC graduation project and 30 EC of free electives. Open Universiteit offers part-time study with flexible pacing and course-specific start dates.
components: Choose eligible courses inside or outside computer science.

core: Programming, software design, algorithms and formal reasoning
Computer architecture, operating systems, networks, databases and security
Mathematical foundations and academic computer-science research
Artificial intelligence and data in the computer-science curriculum
adjacent: Information systems, users and organisational technology
Societal effects, ethics and communication of digital systems
questions: How can reliable, secure software and computer systems be designed and maintained?
How can information systems connect data, user needs and organisational decisions?

alternatives.label: Computer Systems, Software and Algorithms
alternatives.concept: Learn to program, develop software and design algorithms. Study networks, operating systems and databases alongside the mathematics used in computing. Apply these foundations to machine learning and other AI methods. Open Universiteit offers a longer software engineering sequence and dedicated courses in architecture, security and testing.
alternatives.labelReason: Learn to program, develop software and design algorithms. Study networks, operating systems and databases alongside the mathematics used in computing. Apply these foundations to machine learning and other AI methods. Open Universiteit offers a longer software engineering sequence and dedicated courses in architecture, security and testing.
progression: Programming and logic precede algorithms, which precede Advanced Algorithms. Calculus precedes later mathematics, and introductory data study and machine learning precede deep learning.

alternatives.label: Information Systems and Digital Organisations
alternatives.concept: Learn programming, databases and data analysis, then explore how organisations choose and use digital systems. Use product design, user research and digital strategy to study how technology meets organisational needs and affects people.
alternatives.labelReason: Learn programming, databases and data analysis, then explore how organisations choose and use digital systems. Use product design, user research and digital strategy to study how technology meets organisational needs and affects people.
progression: Programming precedes networks and algorithms. Business and product foundations precede digital strategy, while research methods precede organisational behaviour and market research. Data foundations and machine learning precede deep learning.
alternatives.distinctness: Each option has 9 courses absent from the other. This option develops organisational strategy, product and user inquiry and technology adoption; the closest option develops software, advanced algorithms and mathematical foundations.

selection.assessment: Two distinct plans are supported. The closest develops computing systems, software, mathematics, algorithms and applied AI. The related option uses a smaller computing core to study information systems in organisations, digital strategy and users. Networks & Operating Systems provides a substantive introduction to communication technology, while algorithmic work touches cryptography and Ethics of AI addresses privacy. These pieces cannot sustain separate plans in network infrastructure or cybersecurity.

blocks: UCR covers finite automata and computability in algorithms. Open Universiteit devotes a course to formal languages and automata.
Open Universiteit develops object-oriented programming across multiple courses.
Both introduce computational problem solving. UCR focuses on programming in Python.
Both study matrices, vectors and linear transformations. UCR covers probability separately in the computing plan.
Both study logic, sets, relations and formal reasoning.
Both teach object-oriented programming, including classes and inheritance. Open Universiteit extends it across several courses.
Open Universiteit integrates design and implementation in a foundation practicum.
UCR introduces multiple programming styles in Software Development. Open Universiteit also provides a dedicated study of programming languages.
Both study data structures, algorithm design and efficiency.
UCR introduces Haskell and functional programming within Software Development. Open Universiteit gives this subject its own course.
Open Universiteit studies distributed algorithms in a dedicated course.
UCR covers introductory logic. Open Universiteit extends formal logic in a separate computing course.
UCR studies development practices in one course. Open Universiteit offers a separate software engineering course.
UCR introduces debugging and testing in Software Development. Open Universiteit offers a dedicated testing course.
Open Universiteit studies computer hardware and architecture in a dedicated course.
Both study internet architecture and network protocols. The UCR course also covers operating systems.
Open Universiteit teaches object-oriented analysis and design. UCR’s product course addresses user needs and prototyping.
Both study relational database design and SQL.
Open Universiteit brings advanced computing skills together in a team app project.
UCR covers scheduling, processes and memory in Networks & Operating Systems. Open Universiteit provides a separate operating systems course.
Both develop audience-oriented communication. Open Universiteit sets its work in professional computing practice.
Open Universiteit offers dedicated work on representing domain knowledge through ontologies.
Open Universiteit teaches computer security in a dedicated course. UCR touches on privacy and related issues across several courses.
UCR Machine Learning shares predictive methods. Open Universiteit’s AI course also includes other approaches to intelligent systems.
Open Universiteit requires scientific writing as a separate course. UCR develops academic writing across the plan.
UCR addresses how digital systems serve organisations through several courses in its second plan.
Prepare a research plan after the foundation and at least 12 specified advanced courses.
Open Universiteit sets aside 30 EC for free electives.
Open Universiteit requires a supervised 15 EC project. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.

notes.text: Both universities teach programming, algorithms, networks and databases. Open Universiteit provides more dedicated coursework in programming languages, architecture, security and software testing, and requires a supervised graduation project. The second UCR option focuses on how people and organisations use digital systems.

audience.programmeDescription: This Dutch-taught, part-time degree at Open Universiteit covers software, information systems, computer networks and the mathematics behind computing.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The 2026–2027 curriculum includes a 60 EC foundation, advanced compulsory courses, a 15 EC graduation project and 30 EC of free electives. One UCR plan focuses on software, systems and algorithms. The other applies computing to digital strategy, user needs and organisations.
